title: Biodynamic Analysis of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis and Its Vibration-Induced Damages
author: Junde Xie
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jqicmue

steps.title: Import CT and extract vertebrae
steps.instruction: Import the patient’s CT images into MIMICS and selectively edit the data to isolate and extract the vertebrae model.

steps.title: Optimize vertebrae surface
steps.instruction: Load the extracted vertebrae model into Geomagic Studio and perform surface optimization to improve mesh quality.

steps.title: Generate cortical/cancellous and disc
steps.instruction: Import the optimized vertebrae model into 3‑matic; segment the vertebrae into cortical and cancellous bone, create the intervertebral disc geometry, and generate a volume mesh for both vertebrae and discs.

substeps.instruction: Segment vertebrae into cortical and cancellous bone
Create volume mesh for vertebrae and discs

steps.title: Assign material properties
steps.instruction: Import the volume‑meshed vertebrae and disc model into MIMICS and assign the appropriate material properties to cortical bone, cancellous bone, and disc components.

steps.title: Setup FEM and run analyses
steps.instruction: Import the fully edited spinal model into Abaqus, apply constraint conditions and contact interactions, add ligament elements, then conduct model validation followed by modal and harmonic analyses.
